title: Reverse Words in a String
source: canonical Reverse Words in a String concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is a string s of lowercase words separated by spaces. The spaces may be irregular: extra spaces between words, or leading and trailing spaces. Return the words in reverse order, joined by exactly one space, with no leading or trailing space. A word is a maximal run of non-space characters.
constraints: s consists of lowercase letters and spaces

examples.explanation: Word order reverses and the irregular spacing collapses to single spaces.
One word stays one word; stray spaces are trimmed.

hints: First split the input into clean words, ignoring every run of spaces; reversing afterwards is the easy part.
Python gives you split() with no argument to drop all whitespace runs, and " ".join() to rebuild with single spaces.
Return " ".join(reversed(s.split())). If you build the word list by hand, two pointers swapping ends reverse it in place.
solution: Split on whitespace to get the words, reverse the list, and join with single spaces. s.split() with no arguments handles repeated, leading, and trailing spaces at once. Linear time and linear space for the word list.
failureHint: hidden tests include leading and trailing spaces, repeated spaces, and a single word

visible.failNote: collapse every run of spaces to one
